hints.title: Rename the powers
hints.body: Let a=2x and b=2y, both positive. The equations become a+3b=3 and a2−9b2=6.
hints.recap: A repeated exponential substitution can turn simultaneous equations into algebra.
hints.pause: Factor the second equation as a difference of squares.

recall.reminder: A repeated exponential substitution can turn simultaneous equations into algebra.

hints.title: Use the known factor
hints.body: Since (a+3b)(a−3b)=6 and a+3b=3, it follows that a−3b=2. Solve this with a+3b=3.
hints.recap: A known factor can reduce the second equation to a linear one.
hints.pitfall: Check that both resulting exponential values are positive.
hints.pause: Find a and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow></math>, then their ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>.

recall.reminder: A known factor can reduce the second equation to a linear one.

hints.title: Recover the difference of exponents
hints.recap: A quotient of same-base powers corresponds to the difference of exponents.
hints.pause: Take a base-2 logarithm of the ratio.

recall.reminder: A quotient of same-base powers corresponds to the difference of exponents.

solution:
Set a=2x and b=2y. Then a+3b=3 and (a+3b)(a−3b)=6, so a−3b=2.

Adding the linear equations gives 2a=5, hence a=52; subtracting gives 6b=1, hence b=16. Both are positive and therefore correspond to real x and y.

At the solution x=p, y=q, we have 2p−q=ab=5216=15. Thus p−q=log215, option F.
